arithmetic.surplus: taken - maintenance_cost, taken = min(income, M*regrow) = min(income, 1.6)
arithmetic.horizon: fixed T = 20000 steps for every point; a point recorded alive is alive at T, and where the arithmetic says the repair cycle is self-balancing this is a horizon-limited confirmation, not proof
arithmetic.none: never repairs, damage reaches the cap at ceil(1/dr), so dead in every point with dr > 0; cause is the earlier clock: damage at ceil(1/dr) or energy at ceil(E0/(maint - taken)) when surplus < 0
arithmetic.all_or_nothing: cadence condition: alive <=> ceil(1/dr) * surplus >= repair_cost <=> rho <= (1 - maint/income) * dr * ceil(1/dr) = upper_edge; above it, death by damage when surplus >= 0 and by energy when surplus < 0
arithmetic.proportional: per-step condition: alive <=> surplus >= dr*repair_cost <=> rho <= 1 - maint/income = lower_edge; above it the reserve drains, it buys only part of the damage, spends everything and dies of energy
arithmetic.P1_none: none alive in 0 of the 40 main points with dr > 0 and rc > 0
arithmetic.P2_all_or_nothing: all-or-nothing alive in 32 of 40 main points (rho <= upper_edge)
arithmetic.P3_proportional: proportional alive in 28 of 40 main points (rho <= lower_edge)
arithmetic.P4_window_differs: lower_edge < rho <= upper_edge only at dr = 0.3, where dr*ceil(1/dr) = 1.2; exactly one of all-or-nothing and proportional lives in those 4 points (income 1.0 and 1.5, frac 0.9 and 1.0); for dr in 0.001, 0.01, 0.1 the two edges coincide and the strip is empty
arithmetic.P5_coincidence: all-or-nothing and proportional are the same run iff rho <= lower_edge (28 of 40 main points): there the all-or-nothing rule repairs every step, which is what proportional does, at the same price
arithmetic.P6_free_repair: repair_cost = 0 with dr > 0 is not 'nothing to repair': repair is free, none refuses it and dies of damage, the two repairing strategies live when surplus >= 0
arithmetic.P7_silent: damage_rate = 0 -> nothing accumulates, the repair branch is never entered, all three strategies are the same run
arithmetic.boundary: equality counts as alive (>=); FINDING-145 measured the cadence equality alive; the code compares price < energy, so the boundary is a floating-point question (core/src/organism.rs); TOL = 1e-12 relative

fires.evidence: 54 of 60 points have strategies with a different lifetime, cause or accumulated energy; 6 points are identical across all three strategies (6 of them because nothing accumulates at damage_rate = 0)

silent.evidence: 6 points with damage_rate = 0 (repair_cost 0 and 1.5, income 0.3/1.0/1.5): in all of them the three strategies have the same lifetime, cause and accumulated energy

specific.evidence: movement is `stay` in every arm and only `--repair` changes; predicted alive/cause mismatches 0/180 and 0; the set of points where all-or-nothing and proportional are the same run is exactly `rho <= lower_edge` (28 measured, 28 predicted, agree=True); the set where exactly one of them lives is exactly the predicted strip (4 measured, 4 predicted, agree=True); the reference point reproduces its dynamics hash on a repeat run: True

verdict.reason: Strategies differ: 54 of 60 points show a different lifetime, cause or accumulated energy, and the difference comes from the repair rule alone (movement `stay`, same world, seed, field and horizon; only `--repair` changes). Alive counts on the 40 main points (dr > 0, rc > 0, income > maint): none 0, all-or-nothing 32, proportional 28 — predicted 0/32/28 with 0 alive/cause mismatches. The living window is not the same for the two repairing rules: all-or-nothing reaches the cadence edge upper_edge = (1 - maint/income) * dr * ceil(1/dr), proportional stops at the per-step edge lower_edge = 1 - maint/income; the two edges separate only at dr = 0.3 (1.2x apart), and exactly the 4 predicted strip points show all-or-nothing alive while proportional is dead of energy (e.g. dr = 0.3, income = 1.0, rho = 0.432: alive at 20000 vs 157 steps; rho = 0.48: alive at 20000 vs 63). Where rho <= lower_edge the two are the same run, measured in 28 of 28 predicted points. Above both edges all repairing strategies die and `none` dies in every point with dr > 0.

limitations: the horizon is fixed at 20000 steps: a point recorded alive is alive at 20000, not proved immortal. The FINDING-145 per-point bound is not used because it bounds a dying point, not a self-balancing cycle — at dr = 0.3, rc = 1.44 it says 204 steps and the organism is alive after 200000.

one organism on a uniform field, no competition, no sharing, no memory; movement is `stay` in every arm, so the movement axis is not measured at all here. The difference measured is the difference between the three repair rules under that one movement policy.

the grid is 4 damage rates x 3 incomes x 5 rho fractions of the cadence edge: the strip where the two edges separate is one `dr` wide (dr = 0.3), so the measured difference between all-or-nothing and proportional rests on 4 points out of 40. That is the arithmetic of the model, not a chosen grid: for dr = 0.001/0.01/0.1, dr*ceil(1/dr) = 1 and the edges coincide.

equality at both edges counts as alive with a 1e-12 tolerance; the code compares `price < energy`, and core/src/organism.rs records that this boundary is a floating-point question, so a neighbouring point is needed to tell `>=` from `>`.

per-point table only as far as `points`: the numbers are lifetime, cause and accumulated energy per strategy, not the trajectories. Two arms declared the same run are compared on those three fields, not on a full trace hash at each point.

`proportional` in `core` is the repaired-amount rule with the charge clamped; it is not the older `worst`/`round`/`cheapest` of the FINDING-143 mock, so nothing here transfers to those rules or to segment damage.
